Subject: Re: Quick Q on where customer data is actually processed

Ben —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answer up front: for Redwood's hosted API we execute inference in the region selected by routing policy (by default, requests are routed to the nearest available region), and we have documented fallbacks that may route to an adjacent region if capacity is constrained. We do not persist request payloads beyond configured retention windows and we provide customer options to pin execution to specific regions for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Deliverables attached: a high-level processing map (redwood-processing-map-20270621.pdf), an anonymized subprocessor inventory (subprocessor-inventory-20270621.csv) and a redacted SOC 2 Type II we can share with procurement (soc2-type2-redacted-2027.pdf).

Key points:  
- Regions we operate in (hosted): us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, europe-west4, asia-southeast1 (region list can be tailored per account).
- Routing policy: latency-first by default; customers can change to region-pin or cost-tier.
- Cross-border transfers: transient execution handoffs occur when we route to a non-origin region for capacity/latency reasons; we log these handoffs and can produce an execution trace for a sample window.
- Subprocessors: cloud infra (major CSPs), observability provider (traces/metrics), logging/backup provider (encrypted). Inventory attached includes service role and location.

Marissa, Karthik — copying you for any technical evidence FinFlow needs (e.g., sample trace output, CSV of request hops, or an internal runbook snippet).

We can also open an evidence pack in Drive and a short walk-through call if FinFlow's security wants a live review.

—Michael
Michael Grant

If you can provide the trace and a short note on encryption/handle-level access, we can move to the legal redlines prep. Also, is there any need for a DPA addendum for cross-border operations or do you cover that in your standard DPA?

Thanks —

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick Q on where customer data is actually processed

Hi Ben,

Following up with the technical evidence you requested. See the summary below and the files in the shared Drive link Michael included. If you'd like, we can produce a short sample trace for a time window you specify (we typically provide a 24-hour anonymized trace with request IDs removed).

Summary:  
- Sample trace: an example we provide redacts PII and strips prompt tokens; it shows origin UTC timestamps, regional ingress (eu-west-1 -> us-west-2), internal routing decision (capacity-based fallback), and the final inference host. We do not include customer prompt content in traces — only metadata (region, timestamps, model version, and anonymized request hash).
- Caching/KV exposure: prefix and KV caches are stored encrypted at rest; caching layers run in the same tenant-isolated runtime when Dedicated, and in the hosted case caches are sharded and encrypted; cache operators do not have access to plaintext prompt content. Only the inference runtime operates on decrypted input in memory, and we maintain memory hygiene to avoid persistent plaintext storage.
- DPA: Redwood's standard DPA includes cross-border processing clauses and SCC/adequacy references where applicable. For enterprise accounts we offer a DPA addendum that can specify region pinning or additional execution residency guarantees as a contractual term.

Next steps we recommend: 1) We can produce an anonymized 24h trace; please confirm the date range. 2) If FinFlow requires strict EU-only execution, we can propose region-pin Dedicated capacity pricing and a DPA addendum to reflect the contractual residency guarantee.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments provided in Drive: anonymized-exec-trace-sample.csv (redacted), dataflow-diagram.png
